## Natural history notes

A large leaf-footed bug characterized by its elongated brown body, long antennae, flattened leaf-like expansions on the hind legs, and widened hind femora with spines. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, citrus groves, and other areas with shrubs, trees, vines, and herbaceous plants. It feeds by piercing plant tissues and sucking sap from stems, fruits, seeds, and new growth, and may sometimes be noticed on ornamental or crop plants while also serving as prey for birds, spiders, and predatory insects.
